lines.text: This is a compressor, one of hundreds of machines that keep a chemical plant running. When it stops, production stops too.
For weeks, this one had been shaking a little harder. Then, one day in April, it hit its safety limit and shut itself down. Thirty-two hours offline, and about one point six million dollars lost.
So, why did it happen? To find out, an engineer has to dig through four different files. And they don't even agree. One says the alarm limit is sixty. Another says forty-five.
So the machine gets fixed, it runs again, and the case looks closed. But the steps that would stop it from happening again? Still not done.
So we built PlantPulse on one simple rule. Check the pulse, not just the patch.

One overview shows all three hundred eighty incidents across twelve plants, plus five root-cause cases. Real losses and possible losses are kept separate, and every machine is checked against its own limits.
The Problem Tank ranks all two hundred twenty open issues by risk and due date. Our compressor is first in line, with four fixes overdue.
Every number links back to where it came from. And when two sources disagree, PlantPulse flags it and gives it an owner, instead of quietly picking one.
In Investigation, a quick checkup shows every reading on the part where it's measured. All four readings look fine. But only one of six follow-up actions is done, and just five of eleven checks pass.

Next, the AI investigator ranks the likely causes, finds similar past incidents, and writes a draft report. Then an Evidence Guard checks every sentence. If a number isn't in its source, the sentence gets flagged. In our internal blind test, the real cause came out on top in seven of nine runs, and in the top three every time.

Then it turns into action. Every fix gets an owner, a due date, and the proof needed to close it. Try to close it without proof, and PlantPulse says no. Someone other than the owner has to sign off, and every decision is saved in a log that can't be quietly changed.

Behind the scenes, sixteen source files pass six quality checks and land in one clean data model. Every headline number is checked against its source, and all twenty-three checks pass. PlantPulse only reads plant data, never changes it, keeps a person in every decision, and only claims what it can measure.
PlantPulse. Check the pulse, not just the patch.
